name: Densor Notation
author: Dirk
description:
"Densor Notation" is a pun on "Tensor Notation" used in Tensor Calculus. 
The notation is a work in progress, and I plan to update it as I go (:
I would love input form my betters on how these variables may be designated.
image_code:
//////////////////////////////
    //                          //
    //  DIRK'S DENSOR NOTATION  //
    //                          //
    //////////////////////////////


    #define  loop mainImage

    #define  iR iResolution
    #define  iM iMouse
    #define  iT iTime
    
    #define  v2 vec2
    #define  v3 vec3
    #define  v4 vec4
    
    #define  i2 ivec2
    #define  i3 ivec3
    #define  i4 ivec4
    
    #define  m2 mat2
    #define  m3 mat3
    #define  m4 mat4

    #define  A  abs
    #define  B  break
    #define  C  clamp
    #define  D  dot
    #define  E  floor
    #define  F  float
    #define  G  texelFetch(iChannel0,i2(xy),0)
    #define H(k) texelFetch(iChannel1,i2(k,0),0)
    #define  I  int
    #define  J  
    #define  K  fract
    #define  L  length
    #define  M  max
    #define  N  normalize
    #define O(c) for( i=0; i<c; i++ )
    #define  P  pow
    #define  Q  mix
    #define  R  return
    #define  S  step
    #define  SS smoothstep
    #define  T  texture( iChannel2, p )
    #define U(p) (2.0*p-iR.xy)/iR.y
    #define  V  void
    #define  W  min
    #define  X  cross
    #define  Y  mirror
    #define  Z  reflect


V loop( out v4 pixar, in v2 pixel )
{
    v2 uv = (2.0*pixel-iR.xy)/iR.y;
    v2 uv2 = K( sin( iT+uv*3.0+cos(iT*2.7+uv))+uv*10.0)-0.5;
    
    F f = L( uv2 ) - 0.01;
    f = SS( 0.02, 0.03, f );

    v3 c = v3( 0.0, 0.7, 0.0 )*( 0.5 + 0.5*f );

    pixar = v4(c,1.0);
}
